patch.value:
CodeRabbit, Major, test/verify-release-publish-attestation.test.ts:1072-1081 (PR 84):

"**Add a positive assertion that the heredoc actually terminates.** — Each heredoc test expects one failure. That result holds in both directions: if the heredoc closes, `FLAG` is scoped out and `npm publish \$FLAG` fails; if the heredoc never closes, `FLAG` is also unindexed and the same publish fails. So these cases do not prove that the indented terminator ends the payload.

Assert the closing behavior directly by indexing a scalar after the terminator. This is the coverage that would expose the termination gap reported at scripts/shell-command-scan.ts lines 634-637."

The same vacuity was confirmed in a third heredoc test ("heredoc payload syntax does not change scalar scope"), which shares the criterion: its heredoc never closes under any correct implementation of shell semantics, so scope stays trivially unchanged. All three received the same treatment.
Two heredoc regression tests assert a failure that holds whether or not the heredoc terminator is recognised

CodeRabbit Major on PR 84: the heredoc tests expect one failure that holds in both directions, so they would pass against a scanner that never terminates heredocs at all — coverage that reads as coverage but proves nothing.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text:
Confirmed the vacuity by tracing both directions. Each heredoc fixture's terminator line was written with 10 spaces of indentation and no run: block header, so under correct shell semantics the heredoc NEVER closes: if it closed, FLAG was payload and npm publish $FLAG failed; if it never closed, FLAG was equally unindexed and the same publish failed. Both directions yield the asserted single failure, so the tests would pass against a scanner that never terminates heredocs at all — and the fixtures were not realistic shell (an indented terminator is not a terminator in bash) nor realistic YAML (no run: header to own the indentation).

Fix: all three heredoc tests now use a realistic run: | block (workflow path .github/workflows/release.yml) whose block indentation is stripped before the scan — the text bash actually receives — and each routes its publish through a scalar assigned AFTER the terminator ($NPM publish $FLAG). One assertion now discriminates three wrong implementations at once: terminator unrecognised -> the publish is omitted and the attested sibling returns 0 failures; payload indexed -> the publish reads attested and returns 0 failures; terminator recognised and payload kept as data -> exactly 1 failure naming the missing flag. A scalar-level assertion (shellScalars(dedentRunBlocks(text)).get("NPM")) pins the same property directly.

value.note: dedentRunBlocks used by the restructured fixtures
three heredoc tests restructured with positive post-terminator assertions

value.command: npm test -- --test-name-pattern "a numeric heredoc delimiter keeps its payload as data"
npm test -- --test-name-pattern "multiple heredoc payloads all remain data"
npm test -- --test-name-pattern "heredoc payload syntax does not change scalar scope"

patch.value: The numeric-delimiter, multiple-payload and payload-scope heredoc tests now use a workflow run block whose YAML indentation is stripped before the scan (the text bash receives), keep their original payload-stays-data intent, and add the positive assertion CodeRabbit asked for: a scalar assigned after the terminator is indexed and routes the audited publish, with a shellScalars(dedentRunBlocks(text)) assertion pinning the same property at the scalar level. A third test sharing the vacuity criterion (heredoc payload syntax does not change scalar scope) was given the same treatment.

Each restructured test must fail when the terminator is not recognised (the publish is omitted and the attested sibling returns zero failures), fail when payload is indexed as scalar (the publish reads attested), and pass only when the terminator is recognised AND the payload stays data (exactly one failure naming the missing flag).

Revert-proof by hand: reverting the dedent to an identity function reddened exactly the three restructured heredoc tests plus the run-block bypass regression and the dedent unit test (92 pass / 5 fail across the two suites, every pre-existing test green); restored, 97/97. npm run coverage 100/100/100; npm run check, npm run docstring and npm run release:check green. pm test --run collides with this repository's own pm-integration tests inside the linked-test sandbox (pre-existing, files untouched by this change); every linked command was executed directly and observed green, including single-title runs.

All three heredoc tests restructured onto realistic run: | fixtures whose publishes route through post-terminator scalars, so each assertion now fails unless the terminator is recognised and fails again if the payload is indexed - the vacuity is gone in both directions.
